text: Nationwide Mut. Ins. Co. (9th Cir. 1997) 109 F3d 642, 647 (applying Calif. law); Golden Eagle Ins. Corp. v. Rocky Cola Café, Inc. (2001) 94 CA4th 120, 128, 114 CR2d 16, 22—exclusion applies only to liability flowing from insured employer's acts in the context of and related to injured person's employment] [3:392] Reserved. • [3:393] A defamation claim based on statements to customers regarding an ex-employee who had gone into competition with the employer was not “employment related.” The statements were in response to accusations by a competitor (the ex-employee) and thus related to competition in the marketplace rather than the former employment. [HS Services, Inc. v. Nationwide Mut. Ins. Co., supra, 109 F3d at 647 (also holding “chain of causation” broken 6 between termination and defamatory remark)] • [3:394] Waitress (plaintiff) claimed Manager had coerced her into a sexual relationship and that after she terminated their relationship and quit her job, he followed her to a gym and called her a “sexually promiscuous and calculating bitch.” She sued Manager and Employer on several theories, including defamation.
